key_insight: PV disaggregation from net smart meters works best when the model is evaluated in the same deployment regime it was trained for, because customer transfer and temporal extrapolation affect accuracy more than architecture choice.
engineering_relevance: Distribution operators can use regime-matched error budgets, choose context windows by use case, and fine-tune with a small number of target households to improve behind-the-meter PV visibility in new regions.
method: Defined four deployment regimes separating household transfer from future-period extrapolation.
Benchmarked representative deep sequence models on Ausgrid smart-meter data with adaptation to Pecan Street.
Compared performance under a fixed training protocol and fixed 48-hour context length.
evidence_signal: At 48 hours of context, the best model's daylight MAE increased from 0.104 kW on seen households to 0.185 kW on unseen households, and five target-household fine-tuning reduced transfer error by 28%–36%.
watch_item: Cross-region deployment still depends on limited target-data availability, and longer input windows do not help all models equally for new-customer transfer.
paper_title: Behind-the-Meter Photovoltaic Visibility from Net Smart Meters: Deployment Regimes and Operational Insights
